culture-on-the-land-sequent.alt: Three drawings of one invented riverbank. About 1850: a fishing camp of wooden lodges, a drying rack and a canoe. About 1920: a brick mill with a smokestack, a rail line and small workers' houses. About 2020: the same mill, now lofts and a cafe, keeps its smokestack beside a glass tower and a riverside path. Each period left marks that the next one built on.

culture-on-the-land-street.alt: A drawn street in a Vietnamese American neighborhood such as Little Saigon in Westminster, California. Signs in Vietnamese and English: a noodle house (Phở Saigon), an Asian market (Chợ), a Buddhist temple (Chùa) with a curved red tile roof, a tailor for áo dài (a long Vietnamese dress) and a bánh mì shop, and a community center. People walk on the sidewalk.

culture-on-the-land-1925.alt: Scene 1, Main Street of an invented river town in about 1925: a white wooden church with a steeple and cross, a general store with the sign "Lindqvist & Sons General Store", a brick flour mill with a smoking smokestack, and two small workers' houses. A horse pulls a cart on the dirt street and two people walk past. Every sign is in English.

culture-on-the-land-2025.alt: Scene 2, the same Main Street in about 2025: the church still stands; the general store building is now "Hilal Halal Market" and a Somali restaurant; the flour mill keeps its smokestack but is now "Mill Lofts and Coffee"; the workers' houses are gone and a building holds a "Global Burger" chain restaurant and a "Phones 5G" store. Cars drive on a paved street and people walk past.
